title: Research: complex copy budgets for 3-6 unpaid coordinates with large local children (planning screen; no κ)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution -->
_Requested by **Mark**_

## Change and mathematical scope

**Planning screen, no construction, supplier or κ claim.** This package gives certified complex decoder copy budgets for coverage laws with **u = 1..6 unpaid coordinates per family**, with the shipped word or with all non-copy local mass at one large rank (8, 16 or 32). Targets run from the incumbent tie up to κ = 0.1. It generalises `plane-port-copy-budgets` (u = 2 only) and complements `kappa010-complex-lever-floor` (κ = 0.1 only).

Largest copy charge per call (copy rank 8):

| u | delivery | tie | κ×2 | κ×4 | a=1/99 | κ=0.05 | κ=0.1 |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | selected | 160 | 128 | 56 | – | – | – |
| 3 | selected | 264 | 232 | 160 | 96 | – | – |
| 3 | rank 32 | 288 | 280 | 256 | 240 | 32 | – |
| 4 | rank 32 | 384 | 376 | 360 | 336 | 128 | – |
| 6 | rank 32 | 584 | 576 | 552 | 536 | 312 | 64 |

Each extra unpaid coordinate adds about 100 units per call. With the shipped word, a = 1/99 first opens at u = 3. κ = 0.1 first opens at u = 6 with rank-32 delivery. Independent per-port copies (about 112u, PR2203's 224 at u = 2) exceed every tie budget, so a useful realization must share copy work. Passing budgets are necessary targets only. The model uses the favourable data-shrink bracket and idealised single-rank delivery; restoration, hosting, precision and other native costs are unpriced.

## Task and overlap

Card `coverage-law-change` (priority revision 6), scope refined (TASK.json). Base `6f100d4bb`; contribution commit `c574f2e48d21679cd9994894a5e44d84bbbd2c91`. Nearest work: `plane-port-copy-budgets` (u = 2), `kappa010-complex-lever-floor` / `kappa010-rank-cap-floor` (κ = 0.1 thresholds), `complex-coverage-law-relief` (threshold table at other targets). No open PR prices u ≥ 3 budgets across targets (checked over 255 open PRs).

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-multi-unpaid-copy-budgets
```

The registered replay passes locally with Python 3.12.10 (about 3.5 min, standard library only). The engine `complex-local-word-ceiling/ceiling.py` is imported unchanged and SHA256-pinned. Every budget is sharp: k passes and k+1 fails, both certified. Controls: u = 2 reproduces all six of plane-port-copy-budgets' complex shrink cells; u = 1 with the shipped word gives exactly today's 64; a = 1/9 opens first at u = 6 for rank 32, matching kappa010-complex-lever-floor.

## Credit

complex-local-word-ceiling (Douglas Colkitt) and PR1012's coverage identity; ctoth and discussion 1587 for the plane-port contract; JosieElliston's plane-port-copy-budgets method; kappa010-complex-lever-floor; Jeremy Diviney's PR2203 independent-block bill. Prepared by Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code, in a session donated by Mark.

## Open next questions

1. Can a k-dimensional port contract (u = k ≥ 3) be realized with shared copies below these budgets? First step: exact masked fitting ranks for good k-group covers (k = 2 reaches 34 in PR3335), then a native price per shared channel.
2. What are the bit-side budgets for u ≥ 3? First step: rerun the table with `bit-revision3-levers-seed03`.
